description.narrative:
To achieve this Theory of Change, an Intersectional Feminist Political Ecology (FPE) and a Human Rights-Based Approach (HRBA) will be used. These combined frameworks dismantle the political and cultural barriers that silence marginalized groups in transboundary spaces like the Mekong River. Traditional water governance treats climate change as a purely technical engineering issue, prioritizing infrastructure like dams while ignoring social impacts. By contrast, an FPE and HRBA approach proves that water insecurity is a direct result of political, economic, and identity-based exclusion. Traditional gender policies treat women as a single, uniform block. Intersectional FPE dismantles this by showing how environmental damage impacts people differently based on overlapping identities.First, it reveals hidden structural vulnerabilities; for example, when Mekong dams disrupt fish stocks, rural women face a direct increase in unpaid domestic labour to secure food and water. Second, it addresses compounded exclusions, highlighting how a wealthy farmer can buy water pumps during a drought, while an indigenous woman with a disability or a SOGIESC+ individual faces severe discrimination and mobility barriers to accessing relief. Finally, it legitimizes local knowledge, treating the generational resource-management skills of diverse women as vital science rather than optional folk wisdom. A Human Rights-Based Approach (HRBA) transforms climate vulnerabilities from basic needs into enforceable rights. This shifts the status of marginalized women, youth, and SOGIESC+ individuals from passive victims to Rights-Holders entitled to water, food security, and a healthy environment, and thus should be part of policy and decision-making. Simultaneously, it redefines states and transboundary agencies as Duty-Bearers legally obligated toensure transparency and equity. Crucially, HRBA mandates Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC), giving frontline communities thelegal leverage to block top-down infrastructure and demand a permanent seat at the decision-making table. When implemented together, these two frameworks address both the root causes of social inequality and the formal legal pathways needed to achieve systemic justice by preventing maladaptation and securing safe civic engagement.
Activities:
1. Series of Online Learning Sessions with IP3 Country Partners to develop the Mekong Water Governance and Climate Agenda for ASEAN Engagement using feminist analysis (June to December 2026) – Aims to bring togetherthe IP3 partners to share their lived realities from which together they will transform their national Mekong issues into a collective regional agenda using feminist analysis for an inclusive and gender-responsive Mekong River water governance and climateresilience which they will engage with ASEAN, particularly with AICHR, ASOEN, ACWC, and ASEC to influence the development of the Regional Plan of Action (RPA) of the ASEAN Declaration on the Right to a Safe, Clean, Healthy and SustainableEnvironment.
1.1. Online Learning Session Series 1: Sharing of IP3 Mekong country partners 1.2. Online Learning Session Series 2: Navigating the ASEAN for engagement 1.3. Online Learning Session Series 3: Development of an inclusive and gender-responsive Mekong water governance and climate resilience agenda using feminist analysis 1.4. Online Learning Session Series 4: Finalizing the Regional Agenda
The main participants in the learning sessions are the IP3 partners of Oxfam. In the first learning sessions,IP3 partners will share their realities and national agenda on an inclusive Mekong water governance and climate resilience. In the second learning session, IP3 partners will get to know ASEAN, particularly how ASEAN operates as a regional organization, to guide them in their engagement, particularly with AICHR, ASOEN, ACWC, and ASEC. A resource person who worked with ASEAN, particularly AICHR and who had been part of the development of the ASEAN Declaration on the Right to a Safe, Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment will be invited. The third and last learning session will focus on the development of the agenda.
2. Regional Consultation Workshop and Dialogue with ASEAN on Mekong Water Governance (July to September 2026) – Aims to mobilize and organize WROs and CSOs in Southeast Asia on Mekong water governance to develop a unified advocacy voice that will engage with ASEAN, particularly AICHR, ASOEN, ACWC, and ASEC. In this consultation workshop, GEDSI-focused data that proves the link between dam-related river changes and increased gender-based vulnerability (i.e., loss of livelihoods, displacement, migration, food insecurity) will be collected and documented through rapid lived experience mapping to serve as primary evidence for an Inclusive andGender-Responsive Mekong River Water Governance and Climate Resilience Agenda. During this regional consultation workshop, IP3 country partners and regional WRO and CSO networks will builda unified agenda using feminist lens. The draft regional Agendawillbe presented to AICHR, ASOEN, ACWC, and ASEC as marginalized groups’ input for inclusion into the RPA of the ASEAN Declaration on the Right to a Safe, Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment.
2.1. Preparation activities ● Listing of regional WROs and CSOs in Southeast Asia with work on climate, GEDSI, environment, and Mekong ● Designing the Regional Consultation Workshop ● Identifying resource persons ● Online meeting with target participants and resource persons for briefing ● Logistic preparations (air tickets, venue, accommodation, materials) ● Listing of invitees (WROs, CSOs, ASEAN Secretariat, MRC, ACW, AICHR, ASC, APSC, AICHR, ASOEN, ACWC, ASEAN Secretariat) ● Drafting of invitations ● Sending invitations
2.2. Advocacy Agenda Setting: Regional agenda setting after convening and consultation with different regional networks, stakeholders for future advocacy in favour of women leadership in inclusive water governance and climate resilience.
3. Development of Knowledge Product (January – May 2027) 3.1. Written Agenda on Inclusive and Gender-Responsive Mekong River Water Governance and Climate Resilience
4. Representation (June 2026 – May 2027): Champion the priorities of diverse women (indigenous, youth, disabled, and SOGIESC)within regional forums to connect ground-level water insecurities to ASEAN-wide policy perspectives. This is to ensure that transboundary Mekong water governance and climate resilience frameworks are directly driven by frontline community realities.

participating-org.narrative:
The Womens Legal and Human Rights Bureau Inc. (WLB), formerly Women#s Legal Bureau, was established in 1990 by feminist human rights advocates wanting to effectively address the prejudices suffered by Filipino women before the law and in the legal system. WLB emerged as the first consciously feminist legal organisation pushing for feminist legal advocacy as a strategy for the promotion and defence of women#s human rights. Its mission today is primarily to actively engage in advocacy together with other women#s groups to transform the law and the legal system, and engage its institutions, towards the empowerment of women, especially in the grassroots. This is being pursued in furtherance of the right of women to self-determination and the advancement of their dignity, rights and leadership, in concert with national and global movements for alternative development.
WLB and Kalyanamitra will work hand-in-hand inimplementing this project. These organizations have been active within the women#s movements in their respective countries and in SEA for more than two decades. As such, they have consistently applied feminist perspectives in their advocacy works that include educating women#s grassroots organizations, writing modules, and providing trainings on women#s human rights. These, together with their close linkages with women community organizations, show that WLB and Kalyanamitra are equipped with the technical skills and expertise necessary for the realization of this project goals.
Kalyanamitra was established on the 28 of March of 1985, as the first feminist organization in Jakarta, Indonesia. To achieve its long-term vision to create community and state system with gender equality and justice through strengthening the capability of women with the principle of care and solidarity, Kalyanamitra has four missions : (1) To strengthen the facilitated community to be a social actor in their area through providing and spreading information and knowledge and critical education; (2) To do studies based on community facilitation to be a recommendation for policy change; (3) To improve public awareness about gender injustice issue; (4) To develop public policy advocacy that has gender perspective. Since its establishment, Kalyanamitra as has accumulated a lot of experience for conducting research, capacity building and developing training module on gender, feminism and CEDAW, advocacy and campaign on the issue of Violence Against Women, and community organizing of women's groups.
Both WLB and Kalyanamitra are members of the Weaving Women#s Voices in Southeast Asia (WEAVE) since 2014. WEAV is a feminist regional network of women#s organizations and advocates working at the national level in six countries in Southeast Asia.
